scene.label: Act 4, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Milan. The court of the Duke's palace
scene.location: Milan. The court of the Duke's palace

lines.text: Already have I been false to Valentine,
lines.plainText: Already have I been false to Valentine

lines.text: And now I must be as unjust to Thurio.
lines.plainText: And now I must be as unjust to Thurio

lines.text: Under the colour of commending him,
lines.plainText: Under the colour of commending him

lines.text: I have access my own love to prefer.
lines.plainText: I have access my own love to prefer

lines.text: But Silvia is too fair, too true, too holy
lines.plainText: But Silvia is too fair too true too holy

lines.text: To be corrupted with my worthless gifts.
lines.plainText: To be corrupted with my worthless gifts

lines.text: When I protest true loyalty to her,
lines.plainText: When I protest true loyalty to her

lines.text: She twits me with my falsehood to my friend;
lines.plainText: She twits me with my falsehood to my friend

lines.text: When to her beauty I commend my vows,
lines.plainText: When to her beauty I commend my vows

lines.text: She bids me think how I have been forsworn
lines.plainText: She bids me think how I have been forsworn

lines.text: In breaking faith with Julia, whom I loved;
lines.plainText: In breaking faith with Julia whom I loved

lines.text: And notwithstanding all her sudden quips,
lines.plainText: And notwithstanding all her sudden quips

lines.text: The least whereof would quell a lover's hope,
lines.plainText: The least whereof would quell a lover's hope

lines.text: Yet, spaniel-like, the more she spurns my love,
lines.plainText: Yet spaniellike the more she spurns my love

lines.text: The more it grows and fawneth on her still.
lines.plainText: The more it grows and fawneth on her still

lines.text: But here comes Thurio. Now must we to her window,
lines.plainText: But here comes Thurio Now must we to her window

lines.text: And give some evening music to her ear.
lines.plainText: And give some evening music to her ear

lines.text: How now, Sir Proteus, are you crept before us?
lines.plainText: How now Sir Proteus are you crept before us

lines.text: Ay, gentle Thurio, for you know that love
lines.plainText: Ay gentle Thurio for you know that love

lines.text: Will creep in service where it cannot go.
lines.plainText: Will creep in service where it cannot go

lines.text: Ay, but I hope, sir, that you love not here.
lines.plainText: Ay but I hope sir that you love not here

lines.text: Sir, but I do, or else I would be hence.
lines.plainText: Sir but I do or else I would be hence

lines.text: Who? Silvia?
lines.plainText: Who Silvia

lines.text: Ay, Silvia, for your sake.
lines.plainText: Ay Silvia for your sake

lines.text: I thank you for your own. Now, gentlemen,
lines.plainText: I thank you for your own Now gentlemen

lines.text: Let's tune, and to it lustily awhile.
lines.plainText: Let's tune and to it lustily awhile

content.text: Enter Host and Julia in boy's clothes, as Sebastian.

lines.text: Now, my young guest, methinks you're allycholly. I pray you, why is it?
lines.plainText: Now my young guest methinks you're allycholly I pray you why is it

lines.text: Marry, mine host, because I cannot be merry.
lines.plainText: Marry mine host because I cannot be merry

lines.text: Come, we'll have you merry. I'll bring you where you shall hear music, and see the gentleman that you asked for.
lines.plainText: Come we'll have you merry I'll bring you where you shall hear music and see the gentleman that you asked for

lines.text: But shall I hear him speak?
lines.plainText: But shall I hear him speak

lines.text: Ay, that you shall.
lines.plainText: Ay that you shall

lines.text: That will be music.
lines.plainText: That will be music

lines.text: Hark, hark!
lines.plainText: Hark hark

lines.text: Is he among these?
lines.plainText: Is he among these

lines.text: Ay; but peace, let's hear 'em.
lines.plainText: Ay but peace let's hear 'em

lines.text: Who is Silvia? What is she,
lines.plainText: Who is Silvia What is she

lines.text: That all our swains commend her?
lines.plainText: That all our swains commend her

lines.text: Holy, fair, and wise is she;
lines.plainText: Holy fair and wise is she

lines.text: The heaven such grace did lend her,
lines.plainText: The heaven such grace did lend her

lines.text: That she might admired be.
lines.plainText: That she might admired be

lines.text: How now, are you sadder than you were before?
lines.plainText: How now are you sadder than you were before

lines.text: How do you, man? The music likes you not.
lines.plainText: How do you man The music likes you not

lines.text: You mistake; the musician likes me not.
lines.plainText: You mistake the musician likes me not

lines.text: Why, my pretty youth?
lines.plainText: Why my pretty youth

lines.text: He plays false, father.
lines.plainText: He plays false father

lines.text: How, out of tune on the strings?
lines.plainText: How out of tune on the strings

lines.text: Not so; but yet so false that he grieves my very heart-strings.
lines.plainText: Not so but yet so false that he grieves my very heartstrings

lines.text: You have a quick ear.
lines.plainText: You have a quick ear

lines.text: Ay, I would I were deaf; it makes me have a slow heart.
lines.plainText: Ay I would I were deaf it makes me have a slow heart

lines.text: I perceive you delight not in music.
lines.plainText: I perceive you delight not in music

lines.text: Not a whit, when it jars so.
lines.plainText: Not a whit when it jars so

lines.text: Hark, what fine change is in the music!
lines.plainText: Hark what fine change is in the music

lines.text: Ay, that change is the spite.
lines.plainText: Ay that change is the spite

lines.text: You would have them always play but one thing?
lines.plainText: You would have them always play but one thing

lines.text: I would always have one play but one thing.
lines.plainText: I would always have one play but one thing

lines.text: But, host, doth this Sir Proteus, that we talk on,
lines.plainText: But host doth this Sir Proteus that we talk on

lines.text: Often resort unto this gentlewoman?
lines.plainText: Often resort unto this gentlewoman

lines.text: I tell you what Lance, his man, told me: he loved her out of all nick.
lines.plainText: I tell you what Lance his man told me he loved her out of all nick

lines.text: Where is Lance?
lines.plainText: Where is Lance

lines.text: Gone to seek his dog, which tomorrow, by his master's command, he must carry for a present to his lady.
lines.plainText: Gone to seek his dog which tomorrow by his master's command he must carry for a present to his lady

lines.text: Peace, stand aside. The company parts.
lines.plainText: Peace stand aside The company parts

lines.text: Sir Thurio, fear not you; I will so plead
lines.plainText: Sir Thurio fear not you I will so plead

lines.text: That you shall say my cunning drift excels.
lines.plainText: That you shall say my cunning drift excels

lines.text: Where meet we?
lines.plainText: Where meet we

lines.text: At Saint Gregory's well.
lines.plainText: At Saint Gregory's well

lines.text: Farewell.
lines.plainText: Farewell

lines.text: Madam, good even to your ladyship.
lines.plainText: Madam good even to your ladyship

lines.text: I thank you for your music, gentlemen.
lines.plainText: I thank you for your music gentlemen

lines.text: Who is that that spake?
lines.plainText: Who is that that spake

lines.text: One, lady, if you knew his pure heart's truth,
lines.plainText: One lady if you knew his pure heart's truth

lines.text: You would quickly learn to know him by his voice.
lines.plainText: You would quickly learn to know him by his voice

lines.text: Sir Proteus, as I take it.
lines.plainText: Sir Proteus as I take it

lines.text: Sir Proteus, gentle lady, and your servant.
lines.plainText: Sir Proteus gentle lady and your servant

lines.text: What's your will?
lines.plainText: What's your will

lines.text: That I may compass yours.
lines.plainText: That I may compass yours

lines.text: You have your wish. My will is even this,
lines.plainText: You have your wish My will is even this

lines.text: That presently you hie you home to bed.
lines.plainText: That presently you hie you home to bed

lines.text: Thou subtle, perjured, false, disloyal man,
lines.plainText: Thou subtle perjured false disloyal man

lines.text: Think'st thou I am so shallow, so conceitless,
lines.plainText: Think'st thou I am so shallow so conceitless

lines.text: To be seduced by thy flattery,
lines.plainText: To be seduced by thy flattery

lines.text: That hast deceived so many with thy vows?
lines.plainText: That hast deceived so many with thy vows

lines.text: Return, return, and make thy love amends.
lines.plainText: Return return and make thy love amends

lines.text: For me, by this pale queen of night I swear,
lines.plainText: For me by this pale queen of night I swear

lines.text: I am so far from granting thy request
lines.plainText: I am so far from granting thy request

lines.text: That I despise thee for thy wrongful suit,
lines.plainText: That I despise thee for thy wrongful suit

lines.text: And by and by intend to chide myself
lines.plainText: And by and by intend to chide myself

lines.text: Even for this time I spend in talking to thee.
lines.plainText: Even for this time I spend in talking to thee

lines.text: I grant, sweet love, that I did love a lady,
lines.plainText: I grant sweet love that I did love a lady

lines.text: But she is dead.
lines.plainText: But she is dead

lines.text: [Aside.] 'Twere false, if I should speak it,
lines.plainText: Aside 'Twere false if I should speak it

lines.text: For I am sure she is not buried.
lines.plainText: For I am sure she is not buried

lines.text: Say that she be; yet Valentine thy friend
lines.plainText: Say that she be yet Valentine thy friend

lines.text: Survives, to whom, thyself art witness,
lines.plainText: Survives to whom thyself art witness

lines.text: I am betrothed. And art thou not ashamed
lines.plainText: I am betrothed And art thou not ashamed

lines.text: To wrong him with thy importunacy?
lines.plainText: To wrong him with thy importunacy

lines.text: I likewise hear that Valentine is dead.
lines.plainText: I likewise hear that Valentine is dead

lines.text: And so suppose am I, for in his grave,
lines.plainText: And so suppose am I for in his grave

lines.text: Assure thyself, my love is buried.
lines.plainText: Assure thyself my love is buried

lines.text: Sweet lady, let me rake it from the earth.
lines.plainText: Sweet lady let me rake it from the earth

lines.text: Go to thy lady's grave and call hers thence,
lines.plainText: Go to thy lady's grave and call hers thence

lines.text: Or, at the least, in hers sepulchre thine.
lines.plainText: Or at the least in hers sepulchre thine

lines.text: [Aside.] He heard not that.
lines.plainText: Aside He heard not that

lines.text: Madam, if your heart be so obdurate,
lines.plainText: Madam if your heart be so obdurate

lines.text: Vouchsafe me yet your picture for my love,
lines.plainText: Vouchsafe me yet your picture for my love

lines.text: The picture that is hanging in your chamber;
lines.plainText: The picture that is hanging in your chamber

lines.text: To that I'll speak, to that I'll sigh and weep;
lines.plainText: To that I'll speak to that I'll sigh and weep

lines.text: For since the substance of your perfect self
lines.plainText: For since the substance of your perfect self

lines.text: Is else devoted, I am but a shadow;
lines.plainText: Is else devoted I am but a shadow

lines.text: And to your shadow will I make true love.
lines.plainText: And to your shadow will I make true love

lines.text: [Aside.] If 'twere a substance you would sure deceive it
lines.plainText: Aside If 'twere a substance you would sure deceive it

lines.text: And make it but a shadow, as I am.
lines.plainText: And make it but a shadow as I am

lines.text: I am very loath to be your idol, sir;
lines.plainText: I am very loath to be your idol sir

lines.text: But since your falsehood shall become you well
lines.plainText: But since your falsehood shall become you well

lines.text: To worship shadows and adore false shapes,
lines.plainText: To worship shadows and adore false shapes

lines.text: Send to me in the morning, and I'll send it.
lines.plainText: Send to me in the morning and I'll send it

lines.text: And so, good rest.
lines.plainText: And so good rest

lines.text: As wretches have o'ernight
lines.plainText: As wretches have o'ernight

lines.text: That wait for execution in the morn.
lines.plainText: That wait for execution in the morn

lines.text: Host, will you go?
lines.plainText: Host will you go

lines.text: By my halidom, I was fast asleep.
lines.plainText: By my halidom I was fast asleep

lines.text: Pray you, where lies Sir Proteus?
lines.plainText: Pray you where lies Sir Proteus

lines.text: Marry, at my house. Trust me, I think 'tis almost day.
lines.plainText: Marry at my house Trust me I think 'tis almost day

lines.text: Not so; but it hath been the longest night
lines.plainText: Not so but it hath been the longest night

lines.text: That e'er I watched, and the most heaviest.
lines.plainText: That e'er I watched and the most heaviest
